nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of LDH-FeOOH
nodes.procedure: 0.15 g (0.52 mmol) of Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O, 0.3 g (0.74 mmol) of Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O, 0.3 g (4.99 mmol) of urea, and 0.3 g (8.1 mmol) of ammonium fluoride were dispersed in a mixture of 20 mL of deionized water under vigorous stirring in a 50 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave for 30 min. A piece of freshly treated nickel foam was immersed into the mixture. The reactor was sealed and treated at 120°C for 6 h. After the reactor cooled down naturally, the powder was extracted and washed several times with deionized water and ethanol sequentially. The recovered solid product was dried in a vacuum oven for 6 h, which was heated from room temperature to 100°C under N₂ atmosphere at 100°C for 2 h with an initial heating rate of 5°C/min.

nodes.description: OER performance evaluation with and without premagnetization in alkaline electrolyte
nodes.source_text: Prior to commencing the electrochemical tests, the catalysts underwent magnetization in an external magnetic field with a strength of 0.98 T for a duration of 4 min. The Tafel slope of the unmagnetized catalyst is 111.7 mV/dec, which suggests that the RDS is the first electron transfer step. In comparison, the Tafel slope of the LDH-FeOOH-PM catalyst is 44.6 mV/dec, implying that the RDS is the second electron transfer step. LDH-FeOOH-PM demonstrated a significant improvement, with overpotentials reduced by 40, 66, and 105 mV at current densities of 10, 30, and 60 mA cm⁻², respectively.

nodes.description: In situ ATR-SEIRAS spectroscopy for OER intermediate tracking
nodes.source_text: Prominent signals at approximately 1049 cm⁻¹ corresponded to surface-bound OOH* intermediates. When compared to the nonmagnetized catalyst, it is evident that LDH-FeOOH-PM exhibits a distinct OOH* peak at a potential of 1.50 V vs the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE). Moreover, at higher applied potentials, the OOH* peak intensity increases, signifying a more facile generation of OOH* on the surface of LDH-FeOOH-PM.

nodes.description: Operando DEMS measurement with ¹⁸O-labeled water for OER pathway identification
nodes.source_text: ¹⁸O-labeled LDH-FeOOH and ¹⁸O-labeled LDH-FeOOH-PM were tested in 1.0 M KOH, and only signals of ³⁴O₂ and ³²O₂ were captured. Additionally, the ³⁴O₂:³²O₂ ratios of LDH-FeOOH and LDH-FeOOH-M in each cycle were both closed to the natural abundance of ¹⁸O in the deionized water, suggesting that ¹⁸O in ³⁴O₂ evolution should originate from water and the AEM pathway occurs on LDH-FeOOH and LDH-FeOOH-M catalysts.

nodes.description: Kinetic isotope effect measurement with deuterated electrolyte
nodes.source_text: The corresponding KIE_H/D values were more than 1.5 when the overpotential range is above 0.35 V, suggesting that O-H cleavage may be directly involved in RDS. Meanwhile, the KIE_H/D values of LDH-FeOOH were smaller than 1.5 when the overpotential range is at 0.30 - 0.50 V, i.e., O-H cleavage may not be directly involved in RDS.

nodes.description: Cyclic voltammetry for Ni²⁺/Ni³⁺ and Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺ transition analysis
nodes.source_text: Both LDH-FeOOH and LDH-FeOOH-PM exhibit two oxidation peaks in their cyclic voltammetry (CV) curves. These peaks are attributed to the Ni²⁺/Ni³⁺ (<1.45 V vs RHE) and Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺ (>1.45 V vs RHE) transitions. Notably, the oxidation peak current during the Ni²⁺/Ni³⁺ transition experiences a substantial increase for the LDH-FeOOH-PM sample, signifying the easier formation of the high-valence Ni species (NiOOH) on the catalyst surface due to magnetization.

nodes.description: In situ Raman spectroscopy for surface reconstruction during OER
nodes.source_text: According to the in situ Raman spectra of LDH-FeOOH, two characteristic peaks are observed at ~443 and 526 cm⁻¹ at low potential, which are attributed to the A_lg stretching modes of Ni^II-OH and Ni^II-O for Ni(OH)₂, respectively. With arising potential (OCP-1.55 V vs RHE), the intensity of these two peaks gradually decreased and disappeared at 1.50 V vs RHE. Meanwhile, the two new peaks that appeared at ~471 and 548 cm⁻¹ are assigned to the e_g bending vibration and the A_lg stretching vibration of Ni^III-O in NiOOH, respectively. Interestingly, compared to LDH-FeOOH, the LDH-FeOOH-PM exhibited fast phase transformation.

nodes.description: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy for charge transfer resistance analysis
nodes.source_text: The findings from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) corroborate this trend, revealing reduced transfer resistance (R_ct) and film resistance (R_f) after magnetization.

nodes.description: Stability testing at high current densities
nodes.source_text: LDH-FeOOH catalyst exhibited exceptional stability with negligible voltage loss for over 100 h with continuous operation at a current density of 200 mA cm⁻² and 500 mA cm⁻², respectively.

nodes.description: AEM electrolyzer performance at laboratory scale
nodes.source_text: For (+) LDH-FeOOH||NF (-) after PM, at the total current of 1 A and 2 A, the cell voltages were 1.79 and 1.87 V, respectively, which were notably lower than those before PM (1.85 and 1.95 V, respectively).

nodes.description: AEM electrolyzer stability testing at laboratory scale
nodes.source_text: Good stability was achieved on (+) LDH-FeOOH||NF (-) electrolyzer for over 100 h at current densities of 0.5 A, 1 A, and 2 A.

Under various applied cell potentials, the current densities of the cell with the LDH-FeOOH electrode are obviously higher than the cell with commercial Raney Ni electrodes. After PM, the LDH-FeOOH-PM catalysts show the best OER activity among all catalysts tested, affording current densities that are nearly twice higher than those of commercial RuO₂ over the cell voltage in the range of 1.6 - 2.1 V. It is also notable that the current density gradually decreased over time, suggesting the weakening of magnetization effect on LDH-FeOOH-PM over time. Nevertheless, the full potential of the LDH-FeOOH-PM can be rapidly and repeatably restored by reintroducing the temporary magnetic field every 6 h.
For LDH-FeOOH, no appreciable decrease in current density was observed over 24 h continuous operation at industrial scale.

edges_measured.value: O K-edge, Ni L-edge, Fe L-edge

nodes.source_text: The O K-edge of magnetized LDH-FeOOH-PM displays more intense peaks than its unmagnetized counterpart, indicating an increased degree of M 3d-O 2p hybridization. The Ni/Fe L₃-edge XANES of magnetized LDH-FeOOH-PM exhibit a significant increase in peak intensities, especially, Ni L₃-edge.

nodes.characterization_summary: X-ray powder diffraction analysis confirms LDH-FeOOH contains NiFe-LDH (PDF No. 49-0188) and FeOOH phases (PDF No. 75-1594 and 81-0462 α-FeOOH) with a nearly 1:1 mass ratio and minor 1.4 wt% β-FeOOH impurity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray powder diffraction (XRD) analysis was conducted to validate the crystal structures of LDH-FeOOH, as depicted in Figure S1. The diffraction patterns closely align with the known patterns of NiFe-LDH (PDF No. 49-0188) and FeOOH (PDF No. 75-1594 and PDF No. 81-0462 α-FeOOH).

nodes.characterization_summary: Scanning electron microscopy reveals nonuniform growth of spherical particles interlinked with NiFeLDH nanosheets in the LDH-FeOOH catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images, as shown in Figures S2a and S2b, unveiled the nonuniform growth of spherical particles that are interlinked with the NiFeLDH nanosheets, consistent with previous findings.

nodes.characterization_summary: Transmission electron microscopy shows distinctive thin laminar crystal habit of LDH sheets with well-resolved lattice fringes at 0.268 nm corresponding to (101) planes of NiFe-LDH, and fringes at 0.259 and 0.267 nm attributed to (021) and (101) planes of α-FeOOH and NiFe-LDH, indicating heterojunctions within nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analysis of LDH-FeOOH (Figure S3a) reveals the distinctive thin laminar crystal habit of the LDH sheets and well-resolved lattice fringes with interplanar spacings of 0.268 nm, corresponding to the (101) planes of NiFe-LDH (Figure S3b). In a different region, lattice fringes with 0.259 and 0.267 nm were discerned, attributed to the (021) and (101) planes of α-FeOOH and NiFe-LDH, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy and corresponding energy-dispersive X-ray elemental mapping confirm high distribution of Ni, Fe, and O throughout the LDH-FeOOH catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM images and corresponding EDX elemental mapping further confirmed the high distribution of Ni, Fe, and O, which supports the observations made from SEM (Figure S3c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry determines the mass ratio of Ni to Fe in LDH-FeOOH at approximately 1:2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The mass ratio of Ni to Fe standing at ~1/2 was determined by inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy shows Ni 2p₃/₂ peak at 855.8 eV (positive shift of 0.1 eV from NiFe-LDH), Fe 2p peak at 712.2 eV (negative shift of 0.2 eV from NiFe-LDH), and O 1s peak positive shift of 0.1 eV, indicating electron transfer from Ni and O to Fe and charge redistribution at the LDH-FeOOH interface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Ni 2p₃/₂ peak of LDH-FeOOH was at 855.8 eV, a slight positive shift from 855.7 eV, which is the Ni 2p₃/₂ binding energy of NiFeLDH. This shift signifies notable alterations to the valence state of the Ni species (Figure S8a). Concurrently, the corresponding high-resolution Fe 2p peak of LDH-FeOOH (712.2 eV) displayed a negative shift of 0.2 eV relative to that of NiFe-LDH (712.4 eV).

nodes.evidence_snippet: The typical OOH* intermediates have been tracked to identify the AEM pathway on the LDH-FeOOH surface; ¹⁸O-labeled LDH-FeOOH and ¹⁸O-labeled LDH-FeOOH-PM were tested in 1.0 M KOH, and only signals of ³⁴O₂ and ³²O₂ were captured (Figures 2e and S15). nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2g, the LDH-FeOOH-PM in KOD/D₂O solution exhibited an obvious drop in OER performance compared with the LDH-FeOOH. nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S21, there was no notable alteration in the BET surface area of the catalyst before and after PM, suggesting that the enhancement in the electrochemical active surface area resulting from premagnetization was not attributed to an augmentation in the BET surface area.

nodes.characterization_summary: O K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure shows increased M 3d-O 2p hybridization for LDH-FeOOH-PM with more intense peaks and broadened peak at 534.0 eV indicating increased electronic states in e_g* orbitals. Ni and Fe L-edge XANES show significant increase in peak intensities for LDH-FeOOH-PM, especially Ni L₃-edge, indicating more electron transitions to 3d states and modified 3d band structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Importantly, energy level splitting becomes more pronounced, with all peaks broadening within an energy range of 530.0 eV (O 1s to higher orbitals transition, e.g., O 3p). Consequently, the O K-edge of magnetized LDH-FeOOH-PM displays more intense peaks than its unmagnetized counterpart, indicating an increased degree of M 3d-O 2p hybridization, potentially leading to heightened oxygen electrocatalysis activity. In Figures 4b and 4c, the Ni/Fe L₃-edge XANES of magnetized LDH-FeOOH-PM exhibit a significant increase in peak intensities, especially, Ni L₃-edge, with the high-energy peak and the low-energy peak corresponding to high oxidation state (M³⁺) and low oxidation state (M²⁺), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Density functional theory calculations show that premagnetization induces significant alterations in electronic structure of LDH-FeOOH: O 2p orbital shifts away from Fermi level, M 3d orbital distribution near Fermi level increases with enhanced M 3d-O 2p hybridization. Spin density of oxygen in surface hydroxyl groups shows notable change. For NiFeOOH@FeOOH model, Ni 3d orbitals exhibit denser states near Fermi level after PM, and both Ni and O atoms show accumulated spin electrons aligned in same orientation (spin up), establishing spin conduction channel.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Looking at the projected density of states (pDOS) of LDH-FeOOH before and after PM (Figure 4d), it is evident that the electronic structure of the catalyst undergoes significant alterations following magnification. Specifically, the O 2p orbital exhibits a noticeable shift away from the Fermi level after PM. Additionally, there is a significant change in the distribution of the M 3d orbital near the Fermi level, resulting in an increase in the overlap between the M 3d orbital and O 2p orbital, thereby enhancing the hybridization of the M 3d and O 2p orbitals. After PM, the spin density of oxygen in the surface hydroxyl group of the catalyst shows a notable change (Figure 4e).

nodes.characterization_summary: Long-term stability testing shows LDH-FeOOH catalyst exhibits exceptional stability with negligible voltage loss over 100 h continuous operation at current densities of 200 mA/cm² and 500 mA/cm², demonstrating robust durability for OER applications.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S26, LDH-FeOOH catalyst exhibited exceptional stability with negligible voltage loss for over 100 h with continuous operation at a current density of 200 mA cm⁻² and 500 mA cm⁻², respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Laboratory-scale anion-exchange membrane electrolyzer performance shows LDH-FeOOH-PM catalyst achieves cell voltages of 1.79 V at 1 A and 1.87 V at 2 A total current, significantly lower than unmagnetized LDH-FeOOH (1.85 V and 1.95 V respectively) at 60°C. Stability maintained over 100 h at current densities of 0.5 A, 1 A, and 2 A.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For (+) LDH-FeOOH||NF (-) after PM, at the total current of 1 A and 2 A, the cell voltages were 1.79 and 1.87 V, respectively, which were notably lower than those before PM (1.85 and 1.95 V, respectively). The results strongly support the potential of the PM method for enhancing the alkaline water electrolysis. Good stability was achieved on (+) LDH-FeOOH||NF (-) electrolyzer (Figure S28) for over 100 h at current densities of 0.5 A, 1 A, and 2 A.
